MATCH-072.give: Next party. The cloakroom. I’ll find you by the mink.
MATCH-072.hint: Parties. Not the party itself. The room where everyone leaves their coats.

MATCH-077.tell: I can only let go while I’m telling someone the worst thing I’ve ever seen. Into his ear. All of it. The telling is the release.
MATCH-077.label: Let her tell you everything
MATCH-077.give: Tell me the worst of it. Into my ear. I won’t flinch.
MATCH-077.hint: Talking. Into someone’s ear. The worse the story, the closer I get.
MATCH-077.closer: I’ve seen things at the hospital nobody should. When I tell them, really tell them, all of it, something lets go in me. I need a man who’ll listen to the worst.

MATCH-078.tell: I bet myself at cards. Twice now. I lost both times, and the losing is the thing. The cards going down and the room looking at me as the prize.
MATCH-078.label: Stake her at cards and win
MATCH-078.give: Put yourself on the table. I’m playing to win.
MATCH-078.hint: Cards. High stakes. Higher than money.
MATCH-078.closer: There’s a back room game the Bluebirds’ sons play. I’ve sat in. I’ve put up things I shouldn’t have.
MATCH-078.closest: I’ve put myself up. Twice. I lost both times, and the losing was the thing. I can’t stop thinking about the third.

MATCH-079.tell: I need to be posed and not move. Placed against the glass, told not to speak. If I move, it stops and I’m left there. That’s the part I want most.
MATCH-079.label: Pose her and tell her not to move
MATCH-079.give: Against the glass. Don’t speak. Don’t move. I’ll know.
MATCH-079.hint: Stillness. Being told not to move.
MATCH-079.closer: I model for a painter sometimes. Placed against the window, told not to speak. If I move, he stops. That’s the part I think about after.

MATCH-085.tell: The darkroom. Prints coming up in the tray, faces appearing out of nothing, red light. It’s the only place I can let go.
MATCH-085.label: Tell her you’ll stand in the red light
MATCH-085.give: Red light, the tray, the prints coming up. I’ll be right behind you.
MATCH-085.hint: Red light. Faces coming up out of nothing in the tray. My darkroom is the only place I really relax. Mostly.

MATCH-089.tell: I can only let go on a day I’ve ended someone. A name off a list, a man told he’s finished. I go to bed with it still on me.
MATCH-089.label: Ask who she ended today
MATCH-089.give: Who did you end today? Tell me while it’s still on you.
MATCH-089.hint: Power. Real power. I won’t pretend otherwise.
MATCH-089.closer: Some days I take a name off a list. A man told he’s finished. I go home those nights feeling enormous.
MATCH-089.closest: It only works on a day I’ve finished someone. I go to bed with it still on me. You’re allowed to be afraid of that.

MATCH-203.tell: I can’t let go unless you’ve signed something first. A napkin, a receipt. Your name, in your own hand, handed to me. I keep every one.
MATCH-203.label: Sign something for her
MATCH-203.give: Give me a pen. I’ll sign whatever you put in front of me.
MATCH-203.hint: Signatures. Your name, in your own hand. I keep every one I’m given. Want to give me yours?

postcard.title: The Postcard

hook.mogger: Darling, I have one rule, and I break it for nobody. Before a man has me properly, he writes me a postcard. From a town he has never been to, a town I choose, dated a day I choose, signed with love. Three men have written me one. I married all three. Will you write me the fourth?
hook.normie: A confession, sweet thing. I have one rule. Before a man has me, properly, he writes me a postcard from a town I choose, a town he has never seen, signed with love. Three men have done it. I married all three. Would you write me one?
hook.truecel: Don’t flatter yourself. I have a rule: before any man has me, he writes me a postcard from a town I choose, signed with love. Three men have. I married them. You won’t get that far, but I’m curious what you’d write. Will you?

yes.label: Tell her you’ll write it
yes.player: Send me the card. I’ll write it.

reply.mogger: Oh, good. It comes through your door tomorrow. Write it in bed, darling. That’s the rule.
reply.normie: Tomorrow, through your door. Write it in bed. Sign it properly.
reply.truecel: Fine. It’ll come through your door tomorrow. Don’t make a mess of it.

no.label: Tell her it’s too strange
no.player: A postcard from a town I’ve never been to? That’s too strange for me.

reply.mogger: Strange is the only interesting thing left, darling. Never mind.
reply.normie: Oh. Well. The widower from the casino didn’t think so.
reply.truecel: I didn’t expect much. You’ve met expectations.

card.label: A blank postcard
card.text: A blank postcard of a lake town called {town}, the kind of place with one hotel and a pier. In the corner, in her round hand, a date she has chosen. Underneath: In bed, please. Signed with love. C.

love.label: Write it in bed, signed with love
love.notice: You wrote it in bed, as instructed, and signed it with love. It went back out under your door.

joke.label: Draw a fish on it
joke.notice: You drew a fish on it and wrote wish you were here, sort of. It went back out under your door.

love.mogger: It came. You wrote it in bed, I can tell from the slope of the letters. Nobody has made me wait this well in years. It’s in the album now, darling, next to the engineer’s.
love.normie: It came. You signed it with love. I read it four times and put it in the album, on the page after the engineer’s. You don’t know what that means. That’s all right.
love.truecel: It came. Sweet. I’ve put it in the album under the funny ones. Don’t look so hurt, it’s a compliment, sort of.

postcard.album: My albums. Every card in them was signed with love.
postcard.clue: Every man who wrote Celeste Van Doren a postcard married her and is buried at the Cemetery Chapel with a ribbon on his stone.

after.mogger: The committee has heard your name, darling. I said it to them myself. Sleep well.
after.normie: I said your name at the club today. Just once. People listened.

joke.mogger: A fish. You drew me a fish. I haven’t laughed like that since the rancher fell off his horse. You’re not husband material, darling, and thank heaven.
joke.normie: A fish. Wish you were here, sort of. Well. I suppose that’s honest. The widower from the casino wrote a sonnet.
joke.truecel: A fish. Of course. Don’t write to me again.

late.mogger: No card, darling? The widower from the casino wrote his within the hour. I’ll forgive you. I won’t forget.
late.normie: The card never came back. That’s an answer too.
late.truecel: You couldn’t even manage a postcard. Noted.

deaths: A bottle of very old wine came through the door with a blue ribbon on it. You drank to the fourth husband.
The postcard came back, stamped, from a town you have never been to.
There was a ribbon on your door handle. You never heard the knock.

letter.title: The Letter

hook.mogger: This is mortifying, so I’ll just say it. I can only let go when I’m following instructions. Written ones. What to wear, what hour, what to say at the door. I follow them exactly and then I can stop thinking. Would you write mine?
hook.normie: I’ve never asked anyone this. I can only really let go when I’m following written instructions. The outfit, the hour, the phrase to say at the door. Every word, exactly. Would you write me some?
hook.truecel: I don’t know why I’m asking you. I need written instructions to let go. Exact ones. What to wear, when, what to say. Most men write something stupid. Would you?

reply.mogger: Thank you. Choose carefully. I’ll do every word.
reply.normie: Okay. Choose carefully. I’ll follow every word.
reply.truecel: Fine. Don’t make it stupid.

no.label: Tell her you’re not the type
no.player: I’m not the type to give orders.

reply.mogger: No. Of course. Forget I asked.
reply.normie: That’s all right. I’m a little relieved, honestly.
reply.truecel: No. You wouldn’t be.

label.twinset: Write: the twinset, pearls, and a curtsy
label.window: Write: red lipstick, the window, lamp on
label.phrase: Write: say thank you, sir, and nothing else

player.twinset: The cream twinset. Your pearls. Curtsy when you answer the phone.
player.window: Red lipstick. Stand at your window with the lamp on behind you. Don’t wave.
player.phrase: When you ring me, say thank you, sir. Nothing else. Not one word more.

pick.reply: Written down. Every word. I’ll ring you tomorrow night when it’s done.

twinset.mogger: It’s me. Cream twinset, pearls. I curtsied when I picked up the phone, even though you can’t see me. I did every word.
twinset.normie: It’s me. I’m wearing the twinset. The pearls. I curtsied. I know you couldn’t see. I did it anyway, every word.
twinset.truecel: It’s me. Twinset, pearls, curtsy. I did it. Every word. I feel ridiculous. Don’t laugh.

window.mogger: It’s me. Red lipstick. I’m at the window with the lamp on behind me, not waving. A car slowed down outside. I didn’t move.
window.normie: It’s me. Red lipstick, window, lamp on. I didn’t wave. Someone walked past and looked up. I stayed exactly where you put me.
window.truecel: It’s me. Lipstick, window, lamp. I’ve been standing here an hour. I did it. Every word.

choices.well: Tell her she did it perfectly
choices.wrong: Tell her she got one thing wrong

well.mogger: Perfectly. Say it again. No, don’t, I’ll cry. I’m going to sleep in the pearls.
well.normie: Perfectly. Oh. I don’t think anyone has ever said that to me about anything. Thank you.
well.truecel: Perfectly? Really? Okay. Okay. Thank you. I didn’t expect that from you.

wrong.mogger: One thing. Tell me. No, don’t tell me. Write it down. I’ll do it again tomorrow, right, and every day after.
wrong.normie: One thing? Which? Oh, I hate that. I love that. Write it down and I’ll do it again.
wrong.truecel: One thing wrong. Of course. I did everything you said and it still wasn’t enough. Goodnight.

call.hang: You hung up while I was still standing here in it. Thank you for that, I suppose.

forged.mogger: Your second letter came this morning. Same hand. It said to wear the gray coat and stand at the lodge gate after dark and not to ask why. I did everything it said. Nobody came. Why did you want me there?
forged.normie: Your second letter came this morning. Your hand, I’m sure of it. It said to stand at the lodge gate after dark in the gray coat and not to ask why. I went. Nobody came. Why?
forged.truecel: Your second letter came. Same hand. The lodge gate, after dark, the gray coat. I went. I stood there an hour. Nobody came. Was that a joke?

never.label: Tell her you never wrote it
never.player: I never wrote a second letter, Ruth.
never.reply: Then someone has your hand. Someone very good. I stood at that gate for an hour. I’m frightened now. Thank you for telling me.

claim.label: Tell her you wanted to see if she’d do it
claim.player: I wanted to see if you’d do it.

reply.mogger: You’re a terrible man. I loved every minute at that gate.
reply.normie: That’s cruel. I liked it. I don’t know what that says about me.
reply.truecel: That’s sick. Don’t write to me again.

delphine.never: Don’t be cross, darling. I only borrowed your hand for one letter. It’s a lovely hand. Generous loops.
delphine.claim: You took credit for my letter. Fine. Then you owe me one, and I always collect.

letter.clue: Someone forged your handwriting to send Ruth Calder to the lodge gate after dark; Delphine Moreau can copy anyone’s hand after an hour with a sample.

picture.mogger: So you can see what you made me do.
picture.normie: So you can see I really did it.

letter.missedVm: It’s me. I did every word, exactly, and you didn’t pick up. I’ll try you again tomorrow.

count.title: Match Point

hook.mogger: I need to tell you something and you’re not allowed to be smug about it. I’ve never let anyone tell me what to do. Not my father, not a coach, nobody. I want you to. Ring me, tell me where and how many, and I’ll do it to myself and count them out loud. My safeword is match point. Will you?
hook.normie: Okay. This is hard to say. I’ve never once let anyone give me orders. I want you to. On the phone. You tell me where and how many, and I do it to myself, and count. If it’s too much I say match point and we stop. Would you?
hook.truecel: Don’t make this weird. I’ve never let anyone tell me what to do, and I want to try it with someone who won’t matter. You tell me where and how many, on the phone, I do it and count. Match point means stop. Can you manage that?

yes.label: Tell her you’ll call the count
yes.player: I’ll ring you. I’ll tell you where and how many.

reply.mogger: Tomorrow night, then. I’ll ring you. Be in charge. It suits you.
reply.normie: Tomorrow night. I’ll ring. Match point if it’s too much. I trust you.
reply.truecel: Tomorrow night. I’ll ring. Don’t be pathetic about it.

no.label: Tell her it isn’t for you
no.player: Telling you to hurt yourself isn’t for me.

reply.mogger: Fair. Most men want to be told. You’re a surprise either way.
reply.normie: That’s okay. Honestly, that’s a kind answer.
reply.truecel: Of course it isn’t. Forget it.

open.mogger: It’s me. I lost a set today for the first time in a year. I’m on the bed in my tennis skirt and I’m furious. Tell me.
open.normie: It’s me. I lost a set today. First time in forever. I’m angry and I want to be told. Go on.
open.truecel: It’s me. I lost a set today. Don’t gloat. Just tell me.

open.mogger: It’s me. Training went on for hours and I can barely lift my arm. I’m on the bed. Be careful with me tonight. Tell me.
open.normie: It’s me. I’m sore from training, every muscle. Go easy. Tell me.
open.truecel: It’s me. Everything hurts from training. Don’t overdo it. Tell me.

choices.gentle: Tell her: three, slowly, on her thigh
choices.firm: Tell her: ten, hard, and count every one
choices.stop: Tell her to just lie there and breathe

right.mogger: One. Two. Three. Oh. That was exactly right. How did you know?
right.normie: That was exactly what I needed. I counted every one. I’m shaking a little. In a good way.
right.truecel: Okay. That was right. I hate that you knew.

count.wrong: Match point. Match point. We’re stopping. You weren’t listening to me.

stop.mogger: Just breathe? Fine. That’s the first order I’ve ever liked. I’m breathing.
stop.normie: Okay. I’m lying here breathing. That was kind. I didn’t know I needed that.
stop.truecel: Breathe. Wow. Brave choice. Okay. I’m breathing.

count.hang: You hung up on me mid count. That’s one way to win, I suppose.

picture.mogger: Two nights. I’ve never been told what to do and liked it before. This is for you.
picture.normie: Two nights of you telling me. I’ve never felt so looked after. This is for you.
picture.truecel: Fine. You were good at it. This is for you. Don’t frame it.

count.missedVm: I rang. You didn’t answer. I sat there in my skirt waiting to be told and nobody told me. Don’t do that again.

refusal.title: Refused

hook.mogger: I’ll be honest, because you look like a man who can take it. I pay men to turn me down. I undress, I ask, and they say no. That’s the only thing that does it for me. I’d pay you more than any of them. Would you be the man who says no?
hook.normie: This is going to sound insane. I pay men to say no to me. I ask, and they turn me down, and that’s the only way I can let go. I’d like it to be you. I’ll make it worth your while. Will you?
hook.truecel: Don’t get excited. I pay men to turn me down. I ask, they say no, I go home happy. You look like you’d be very good at saying no to a woman like me. Prove it?

yes.label: Tell her you’ll say no
yes.player: Ask me anything you like. I’ll say no.

reply.mogger: Good. I’ll ask tomorrow. Every no gets a present. They get bigger.
reply.normie: Tomorrow, then. Every time you say no, something comes through your door.
reply.truecel: We’ll see. Tomorrow. Every no gets you something. Try not to cave.

no.label: Tell her you’d rather just say yes
no.player: I’d rather just say yes, to be honest.

reply.mogger: Everybody would. That’s the problem. Never mind.
reply.normie: Oh. That’s sweet. That’s also no use to me at all.
reply.truecel: Of course you would. Goodbye.

asks.mogger: I’m in the suite at the casino hotel with my shoes off. Come up. Please.
asks.normie: I’m at the casino hotel. The suite. Come up tonight. Please.
asks.truecel: Suite at the casino hotel. Shoes off. Come up. I’m asking nicely.

asks.mogger: I’ve sent everyone home. It’s just me, the bath running and the door on the latch. Come up.
asks.normie: The bath’s running and the door’s on the latch. I’m asking again. Come up.
asks.truecel: Bath running. Door on the latch. Second time I’m asking. Come up.

asks.mogger: Last time. I’m begging, which I don’t do. Come up. Please. Say yes.
asks.normie: I’m begging now. Please. Say yes. Come up.
asks.truecel: Last time. I’m begging. Say yes.

afterNo.normie: Thank you. Something’s on its way to you.

gifts.label: A bottle of champagne
gifts.text: A bottle of very good champagne with a gift tag in a firm hand: For the first no. C.

gifts.label: A silver watch
gifts.text: A heavy silver watch in a box lined with blue silk. The tag: For the second no. Don’t wear it to the club. C.

gifts.label: A casino hotel key card
gifts.text: A key card for the casino hotel’s top suite, in a little envelope. The tag: For the third no. You’ll never use it. That’s the point. C.

gaveIn.mogger: Oh. Oh, no. You said yes. Everybody says yes in the end. I thought you were different.
gaveIn.normie: You said yes. It’s over, then. I’m sorry. It was lovely while you said no.
gaveIn.truecel: Yes. Of course. They all do. Don’t message me again.

won.mogger: Three nos. Nobody has ever lasted three. I’m keeping you, and you’re keeping the watch.
won.normie: Three nos. Nobody has ever managed three. I don’t know what to do with you. Keep the key card. Don’t use it.
won.truecel: Three. Fine. You win. Nobody wins. Keep the key card. I mean it, don’t use it.

refusal.picture: The suite. Empty, like you left it.

lines: Did you see the paper? Somebody tipped off the police and they caught the Back Row in the faculty lot. Whoever that was, I’d buy them a drink.
Professor Vale is alive and the Back Row is in cells. Somebody made a phone call. I love a quiet hero.
They arrested students in the faculty parking lot. A plot against Professor Vale. Somebody knew. I keep wondering who.
A volunteer found a bomb under Professor Vale’s car. He was staying with the Bluebirds that night. Somebody warned them.
Professor Vale says he’s unbearably safe. Somebody sent him to the Bluebirds the night before. I want friends like that.
Professor Vale’s car blew up in the faculty lot with nobody in it. He took a cab that morning. Lucky man, or a warned one.
A car exploded on campus and nobody died. Vale took a cab and won’t say why. I believe him, which is the strange part.
They’re holding a vigil for Professor Vale. I argued with everything he ever said. I didn’t want this.
Professor Vale is dead. A car bomb, in the faculty lot. Everyone says they saw it coming. Nobody stopped it.
Poor Dr. Pemberton. He only borrowed the car. He didn’t even like Vale’s speakers.
A lecturer died in a car that wasn’t his. Hal Pemberton. He taught my cousin. Gentle man. Terrible at parking.
A federal inquiry into the Blue Ribbon Foundation. My mother rang me twice about it. She’s thrilled and pretending not to be.
The Blue Ribbon Foundation is under federal investigation. Somebody handed them a file. Very brave or very stupid. Maybe both.
The Blue Ribbon investigation went nowhere. Of course it did. They own half the judges in Sunfall.
Nothing came of the Blue Ribbon case. Elena Cross is still missing and the gala will go ahead next year like nothing happened.
The Sisters sang all night outside a chapel and somebody warned them first. The crescent flyers are gone.
Victoria Blackwood has left town. The goths are pretending they never heard of her. I heard a lot of her.
Half the goth crowd walked away from Victoria Blackwood and stood with the Sisters. Of all people. I loved it.
The Sisters kept a vigil at the wrong chapel. Whatever happened at the other one, nobody’s talking about it.
Something happened at the chapel. Nobody’s saying what. The candles were still burning when the sun came up.
Have you heard about the chapel? No? Good. Neither have I. That’s what everyone says.
That realtor, Olivia Reid, got fired. Showing houses after dark, apparently. Showing them to whom, nobody says.
Olivia Reid lost her job. Something about the judge’s old house. Sunfall loves a scandal it can’t quite describe.
Caroline Prescott’s house on the ridge road made the paper. The judge’s old place. Somebody’s been very busy in it.
The house on the ridge road was in the paper. Caroline Prescott says it was shown in person. She sounded pleased about it.
The society column ran a story about Diana Moore’s telephone friend. The club thinks it’s hilarious. I think it’s a bit sad.
They found that missing woman alive. Somebody tipped off the police. The man in the coyote mask is still out there, though.
She’s alive. The one the coyote man took. I cried in the shower, which is ridiculous. I don’t even know her.
They found her. The woman who went missing. I can’t stop checking my locks.
I keep thinking about that woman they found. And the mask. Who wears a coyote mask?

texts.seen: Did you see the paper? The man in the coyote mask. I think he was on my street last night. It’s probably nothing.
texts.taken: He’s here. The coyote mask. He’s in my kitchen. Please.
texts.rescued: They found me. They said somebody told them where to look. It was you. I don’t know what to say. Come over. I mean it.

nights: You’re the one she texts. She talks about you, you know. She’s fine. She’s with me. You have three nights to find her, and I’ll help, because otherwise it’s no fun. Listen.
Night two. She’s cold, and she’s cross with you for taking so long. Listen carefully.
Last night. Tomorrow I get bored. Listen.
coyote.afterWrong: You sent the police to {place}. That was rude. She heard the sirens going the other way.

choices.beg: Beg him to let her go
choices.police: Tell him the police are coming

coyote.keep: Ha. You want more. Fine. One more, because I like you.
coyote.beg: Begging. She tried that too. It didn’t work for her either.
coyote.police: Are they. Then I’d better move her. There. Now you’ll have to start again.
coyote.missedVm: You didn’t pick up. She was disappointed. Here’s tonight’s for free.

doreen.label: Tell Doreen {first} is at {place}
doreen.right: Sending everyone. Every car I’ve got. Stay by your phone, love.
doreen.wrong: Officers went to {place}. Nothing. Not a thing. Are you sure about any of this?

places.name: the old junction weigh station
clues: Hear that? Engines. Big ones. They never stop out here.
There’s a light that buzzes all night, and a sign telling the trucks how heavy they are.
The trucks pull onto the scale, stop, and pull off again. Every one of them weighs more than she does.

places.name: the quarry
clues: It’s dusty here. She keeps coughing.
Every so often a horn sounds, long, and then the whole ground shakes.
She’s at the bottom of something they dug out of the hill. They blast in the morning.

places.name: the Rialto
clues: It’s dark here, but it’s a dark that used to be full of people.
There’s a stage, and exit signs, and a little square window high up where the light used to come from.
Velvet seats in rows. Nobody’s sat in them for years. She’s sitting in one now.

places.name: the casino parking garage
clues: It’s concrete here, and it hums. Something bright is singing on the other side of the wall.
Cars come and go on the level above. Every one of them lost money tonight.
The jackpot bells come down through the ceiling. She’s counting them.

places.name: the old drive-in
clues: It’s open here. She can see the stars. She’s cold.
There’s a screen as big as a house, blank, and posts with little speakers on them. None of them work.
Row after row of empty parking spaces, all facing the same white wall.

places.name: the canal tunnel
clues: There’s water here. You can hear it, not see it.
It echoes. A tunnel. People jog past overhead and never look down.
The water runs past her feet toward the old pumping house. The joggers will be back in the morning.

seen.title: Man in Coyote Mask Seen on Brown Avenue
seen.summary: Residents report a man in a rubber coyote mask standing in front gardens after dark.
seen.body: Several residents on and around Brown Avenue say a man in a cheap rubber coyote mask has been standing in front gardens after dark, watching windows. Police ask anyone who sees him to call 911 and not to approach him.

taken.title: Woman Missing From Her Home
taken.summary: Police are searching for {name}, last seen at home.
taken.body: Police are searching for {name}, who has not been seen since she sent a message from her kitchen. Her phone is off. Officers want to hear from anyone who saw a man in a rubber coyote mask.

alive.title: Missing Woman Found Alive
alive.summary: {name} was found at {place} after a tip-off. The man in the coyote mask is still at large.
alive.body: Officers found {name} at {place} after a caller told 911 where to look. She is shaken but unhurt. The man in the coyote mask was gone before they arrived, and police say he is still at large.

dead.title: Missing Woman Found Dead
dead.summary: {name} was found at {place}. The man in the coyote mask is still at large.
dead.body: Police found {name} at {place}. Detectives believe the man in the coyote mask is responsible. Nobody has been arrested, and residents are asked to keep their doors locked.

deaths: There was a rubber coyote mask on your pillow when you woke. You didn’t stay awake for long.
The door was open. Somebody was humming in the hallway. Something smelled of rubber.
You heard yipping outside, like a coyote. Then it was inside.

invitation.label: An invitation
invitation.text: Heavy cream card with a gold edge: The Founders’ Ball, at Founders’ Hall, on Day 14. You and a guest. The whole town will be there. Dress accordingly.

news.title: Founders’ Ball Returns to Founders’ Hall
news.summary: The town’s oldest party is back, on Day 14, and everyone who matters has been invited. So, somehow, have some people who don’t.
news.body: The Founders’ Ball returns to Founders’ Hall on Day 14 after two years away. The organizers promise a string quartet, a dance floor and no speeches. Everyone in Sunfall seems to have an invitation, and everyone wants to know who is bringing whom.

ask.label: Ask her to the Founders’ Ball
player: Come to the Founders’ Ball with me.
I’ve got an invitation to the Founders’ Ball and a spare seat. Interested?
The Founders’ Ball. You and me. Say yes.

mogger: Obviously yes. I’ve had a dress waiting for an excuse.
Yes. You’ll be the second best looking person there.
normie: Yes! I mean, yes. I’ve never been. I’d love to.
I’d love to. Pick me up early. I want to see everyone arrive.
truecel: Fine. Yes. Don’t make me regret it.
Okay. Yes. But we leave when I say.

mogger: Someone else asked first. Sorry, handsome.
I can’t. Ask me again next year.
normie: Oh, that’s sweet. I’ve already said I’d go with friends. Sorry.
I don’t think so. Not yet. Sorry.
truecel: No. Absolutely not.
In front of the whole town? No.

arrive.date: A car comes for you at dusk. {first} is already in it, in a dress that makes the driver miss a turn. For the first time in two weeks you leave your room.
arrive.alone: A car comes for you at dusk. For the first time in two weeks you leave your room. You go alone, which is its own kind of statement.

vale.alive: Professor Vale holds court by the bar, telling anyone who’ll listen that Bret Easton Ellis is next. Several people pretend not to hear him.
vale.dead: There’s an empty chair at the top table with a card on it: Professor Adrian Vale. Nobody sits in it all night.

br.success: The Blue Ribbon Foundation’s table is bare. Their place cards are still there, face down.
br.failed: The Blue Ribbon table is the loudest in the room. Every so often one of them looks at you, and smiles.

chapel.stopped: The Sisters sit together near the door, still a little hoarse from singing.
chapel.reconciled: A table of goths and a table of Sisters have pushed their tables together. Nobody can explain it.
chapel.wrong_place: Nobody mentions the chapel. Twice you see someone touch a crescent pendant at her throat.
chapel.ignored: Nobody mentions the chapel. Twice you see someone touch a crescent pendant at her throat.

coyote.saved: {name} finds you on the dance floor and hugs you for a long time without saying anything.
coyote.lost: Someone has left a single white flower by the door for {name}. People step around it carefully.
coyote.atLarge: On the way out, at the edge of the parking lot, a man in a rubber coyote mask stands very still under a streetlight. Then he isn’t there.

town.loved: Half the room seems to know your name. Women you’ve only ever texted wave across the dance floor.
town.mixed: A few women you’ve talked to say hello. One of them pretends she hasn’t seen you.
town.shunned: Several women you matched with turn their backs when you walk past. Word gets around in Sunfall.

date.warm: {first} dances badly and doesn’t care, and at the end of the night she tells you this was the best evening she’s had in years.
date.cool: {first} is polite all night, and leaves a little early. You’re fairly sure she had a good time. Fairly.

scenes.close: It’s nearly light when you get home. Your room looks smaller than you remember.
